chessReplay.accuracyNote: An independent 0–100 score excluding Book moves. Combines winning-chance loss with centipawn loss, even in lopsided positions. Partial scores update during analysis.
chessReplay.reviewFailed: Review was interrupted. You can resume where it stopped.

reasons.book: This move follows a known opening line.
reasons.checkmate: {{move}} is checkmate: the opposing king is in check with no legal defence. The game ends here.
reasons.sacrifice: Even if the opponent takes the piece with {{reply}}, the position stays balanced or favorable.
reasons.best: This was the strongest move Stockfish found in this position.
reasons.excellent: This keeps the evaluation very close to Stockfish’s top choice.
reasons.excellentWithAlternative: This keeps the evaluation very close to {{alternative}}, Stockfish’s top choice.
reasons.good: This gives up little ground compared with the engine’s top choice.
reasons.allowsMateWithReply: This allows forced mate. Stockfish’s line starts with {{reply}}.
reasons.allowsMate: Stockfish found a forced mate for the opponent.
reasons.dropWithReply: This loses about {{drop}} evaluation points compared with {{alternative}}. The best reply found is {{reply}}.
reasons.drop: This loses about {{drop}} evaluation points compared with {{alternative}}.
reasons.weakerThan: This gives up ground compared with {{alternative}}, the engine’s top choice.
reasons.weaker: The engine evaluation worsens after this move.
reasons.great: Finds a critical solution clearly stronger than {{alternative}}, the engine’s second choice.
reasons.missedMate: Misses a forced mate found with {{alternative}}. This does not necessarily mean losing the game.

chessReplay.title: Game analysis
chessReplay.invalid: This game could not be imported. Check the moves or upload another PGN file up to 100 KB.
chessReplay.methodDetails: Each move scores 100 × exp(−loss/25), where loss is the maximum of chance loss and centipawn loss/10. The game score combines arithmetic and smoothed harmonic means. Tactical labels require legal lines. Elo does not affect evaluation. CAPS2 is Chess.com’s methodology. Changing mode restarts analysis; pausing keeps completed moves.
chessReplay.localOnly: Analysis and explanations on your device · no AI API or per-analysis charges.

designSystem.title: Portfolio Design System
designSystem.intro: Explore the visual identity, theme tokens, and interface patterns used in the portfolio and Astra.
designSystem.brandUsage: Use the portfolio logo in navigation and Astra’s avatar in conversations. Lucide icons help identify actions. Give icon-only controls an accessible name.
designSystem.contrastNote: The AA threshold is 4.5:1. Measurements compare solid token colors in the active theme.
designSystem.fonts: The interface uses Inter with a system font fallback. Code and technical labels use JetBrains Mono, Fira Code, or the system monospace font.
designSystem.typeNote: The scale shows the portfolio defaults. On mobile, the hero title uses 52–80 px. The Galo themes adjust the hero.
designSystem.layoutUsage: Use 4–8 px between related elements, 12–16 px in controls and panels, and 24 px between larger groups.

breakpoints.projects: The project header stacks its controls.
breakpoints.mobile: Astra uses tighter margins and the portfolio switches to its mobile layout.
breakpoints.help: Full Astra resources open in a modal panel. In Compact Astra, the panel is always modal.

designSystem.demo: Try the button states and see confirmation in text.
patterns: Use buttons for actions and links for navigation. In Astra’s catalog, describe what each shortcut opens.
Keep keyboard focus visible and let users dismiss modal panels with Escape.
Show a status message during loading or on error. Combine color and text to communicate the outcome.
Respect reduced-motion preferences in portfolio and chat transitions.
designSystem.handoffNote: Shared tokens and controls live in index.css. themes.css defines theme variants, scroll.css lays out portfolio sections, and astra.css styles Astra’s layout and resources.
